question: Is domestic urban relative concentration present across the same international-share growth quartiles used in Fig5?
claim: Most countries in each Fig5 share-growth quartile have declining normalized equivalent city count and increasing Gini; one sufficiently observed country per quartile illustrates different complete annual trajectories.

panels.a: All 76 countries at their unchanged domestic trend coordinates; point colour identifies the exact Fig5 Q1-Q4 group, while quadrant position defines concentration type. The inset retains all 33 points, 16 country labels and two non-crossing leaders.
panels.b-e: Annual R and Gini for Q1 United States, Q2 Poland, Q3 Brazil and Q4 India. All 28 annual observations, square panels and independent y ranges are retained.

grouping: Exact Fig5 membership, 19 countries each. Q1-Q4 rank the fitted 1998-2025 relative annual change in a country's share of worldwide combined international inflows and outflows.
concentration_encoding: Neutral light-grey background in the upper-left quadrant: R trend below zero and Gini trend above zero. Colours do not encode concentration type.
case_selection: Select exactly one country per Fig5 quartile, with at least 100000 full-period domestic events, at least 1000 events in every year and at least 30 positive-flow cities every year. Review complete trajectories to choose contrasting temporal profiles. Prevalence and scatter always retain all 76 countries. Cases illustrate paths, not a representative group average.
data_integrity: Retain all domestic values, point coordinates, quartile memberships and country labels. Highlight the four new cases in the existing main scatter and inset. Join groups by country code, never by point order; never alter data or selectively scale years to create contrast.
statistics: Descriptive 28-year OLS trends and fixed growth quartiles; no statistical significance or causal claims.

background_grid.placement: Continue both the major-tick intervals and their midpoint guides beyond the outermost labelled ticks, stopping at plot limits. Use display-space intervals on logarithmic axes.
background_grid.boundary_text_policy: No added perimeter. Keep all interior grid guides clear of text and legend footprints.
background_grid.boundary_rule: No added perimeter; continue regular interior major and midpoint grids up to plot limits.
